findings.title: Successful cleanup batches are logged as errors with full ID lists
findings.body: Every normal cleanup batch emits `Error` logs even when `err` is nil, and includes the complete batch of annotation IDs. The same happens for the delete and orphan-tag paths. Large configured batches can therefore generate very large error-level log entries for each batch, causing log-volume/cost spikes and potentially triggering error-based alerts despite successful cleanup. These should be debug-level progress logs (and generally avoid serializing all IDs), while actual errors should be logged only when an operation fails.

findings.title: The PR increases the cadence of every cleanup job by 10x
findings.body: Changing the shared cleanup ticker from ten minutes to one minute reruns not only annotation cleanup but also snapshot, dashboard-version, image, invite, short-URL, and query-history cleanup ten times as often. This materially increases database scans, delete load, and background work for all deployments, and is unrelated to splitting annotation cleanup queries. Keep the existing scheduler cadence or make a shorter annotation-specific cadence/configuration if the new cleanup behavior requires faster retries.
